subject: english-literature
title: Power & Conflict Poetry in Action
welcome_lead: Apply your knowledge to three core poems: Ozymandias, London and Bayonet Charge.
meta_desc: GCSE English Literature — close analysis of Ozymandias, London and Bayonet Charge.
final_note: You analysed how Shelley, Blake and Hughes craft images of crumbled power, social oppression and chaotic combat.

concepts.def: Ten-syllable line with alternating stress — heartbeat rhythm
A four-line stanza, common in Blake's London
Hard b/p/d sounds suggesting violence or force
A story told inside another story
Starting a scene in the middle of action

walkthroughs.body_html:
Shelley's sonnet uses a frame narrative: 'I met a traveller from an antique land.'

The 'sneer of cold command' on the statue's face still survives, but the kingdom is 'lone and level sands.' Power is mocked by time.

Blake's four quatrains trudge through London listing suffering.

The repeated 'every' and 'mind-forg'd manacles' show oppression is mental as well as physical. Even the 'Chimney-sweeper's cry' indicts the Church; the 'hapless Soldier's sigh' indicts the Palace.

Hughes drops us in medias res: 'Suddenly he awoke and was running.'

The soldier becomes 'a yellow hare' — animal imagery shows instinct overriding patriotism. 'King, honour, human dignity' are dismissed as 'luxuries' in the chaos of attack.

mcqs.q: What form is Ozymandias written in?

numericals.q: How many lines does a sonnet have?
numericals.hint: Three quatrains plus a couplet, or an octave plus a sestet.

free_texts.q: What Latin phrase means 'into the middle of things' — starting in the action? Two words, no italics.
free_texts.hint: Hughes uses it in Bayonet Charge.
